title: Centralize the minimum-password-length constant shared by the UI validator and LocalAuthService
why: The same conceptual policy (minimum local-account password length) is hard-coded as 6 in the client-side form validator and 8 in LocalAuthService's domain-layer check. Today the two never collide end-to-end — the offline-signup path that reaches LocalAuthService.signUp always passes a synthetic UUID password, never the user-typed one gated by the 6-char validator — but the values being a single conceptual invariant with two different numbers is a landmine for the next call site that wires a real user-typed password through both layers (client says valid at 6-7 chars, domain then throws InvalidInputException).
recommendation: Define the constant once (e.g. alongside LocalAuthService or in a small shared constants file) and reference it from auth_validators.dart.
acceptance_criteria: A single named constant is referenced by both the UI validator and LocalAuthService
A unit test asserts the two validators agree at the boundary length
